entries.reason: The performance-loss problem is directly entailed: the abstract says existing TTA methods design strategies in isolation from training characteristics and that this degrades performance. The computational-overhead item is only weakly evidenced by its quote, which reports that FGA avoids expensive updates and reduces overhead; that is a claimed method benefit, not a direct statement of an unresolved prior-method problem. The abstract does mention overhead reduction, so the issue is narrow rather than wholly unsupported.
entries.limitations: Keep the overhead claim scoped to test-time prompt-parameter updates/TTA as described in the abstract; do not generalize to all prompt updates, all adaptation, or all VLM computation.

entries.reason: The no-joint-optimization problem is directly stated in the abstract. entries.limitations: Scope the second problem to ahead-of-time memory/computing-overhead estimation in the described training systems; avoid claiming that scaled-input estimation is always costly or inaccurate.

entries.reason: Both problems are directly entailed by the abstract: reducing communication is identified as the primary contribution, and the graph-topology-not-fitting-on-one-device condition motivates distributed sampling. entries.limitations: Keep the claim limited to inexact probabilistic zeroth- and first-order oracles in the stated nonlinear equality-constrained stochastic-optimization setting.
